text_fidelity_a:
60 Lumen Theft Proof Rear Bike Light For Bicycle Commuters - Super Bright USB Rechargeable LED Rear Bicycle Light w/ Lifetime Anti Theft Guarantee This is a sturdy light with a metal housing and a very bright tail light. Unfortunately, road vibrations cause the light to shut off. Before I gave up on this light, I tried to keep it on by checking every 10-15 seconds on my 20-minute ride to work. I had to turn the light back on at least 20 times. So aggravating! At least the crappy $10 lights stay on!

I give it 2 stars due to Fortified's stellar customer service. I wrote them about the issue and they mailed me some rubber bumpers to help hold the battery inside the housing. The reason the light shorts out is because the battery slides loosely into a chamber with the light bulb connection at the base. Amazingly minor road vibrations break the battery-bulb connection and the light shuts off, and doesn't come back on.

Fortified has refunded my purchase, which I really appreciate. I believe there is a chance I received a defective product. I cannot say this for sure, as I was offered rubber bumpers instead of a full replacement.

Check one of these out at your local bike shop, and make sure they have a refund policy.

text_fidelity_a: Confidence Fitness Slim Full Body Vibration Platform Fitness Machine, Black My husband and I bought this piece of equipment to add to our existing exercise equipment, and with the hope that it might boost my low bone density a bit.  I've been using it about 3 times a week for several months now, and while I don't think there is any weight loss (did not want it for that anyway), I definitely feel better after I've been on it for 10 minutes.  When I first started using it, I would stand with my feet about 14-15 inches apart, and an hour or so later would feel my back hurting a bit and I couldn't have the speed any higher than about 5 or 6.  So figured out that since this oscillates up and down from left to right (like a superfast see-saw), I would try standing with my feet much closer together.  The up and down movement would be greatly lessened so it wouldn't put so much pressure on the back after the 10 minute stand.  This worked beautifully and now as long as I keep my feet only about 4" apart I can turn the speed up much higher, it seems to eliminate residual stress in my system, and my back does not hurt at all after using it.  So how you place your feet and your posture also is very important in how you will feel after using this vibration plate.  I have yet to get my bone density rechecked so not sure if it has helped that or not, but I really like this machine a lot, am very glad we bought it and plan to keep using it for as long as it lasts.
text_fidelity_b: Confidence Fitness Slim Full Body Vibration Platform Fitness Machine, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Optimus Crux Lite with Tera Solo Cook Set Received it today in preparation for an upcoming trip, so this is coming from one use - lunch time.

Upon opening, the pots and pans are tiny! If you're a large hungry man, you'll need a bigger set unless you just plan on boiling water for dehydrated meals. Handles seem strong enough to lift as much that fits without bending. Pot has 8, 12, 16 ounce markings readable from the inside. Then pan/lid combo is nice, however I'd like to see the pot go up to 24 ounces, with a shallower pan lid. It seems just slightly too deep for a pan.

The stove is a jet burner. It oxidized after the first use, but I didn't buy it for looks so whatever. It puts out a ton of heat. I really like the wide burner instead of a narrow one to prevent hot spots. On a simmer, the flame will heat the entire bottom of this pot set, awesome!

Trial run: couscous with a few fresh veggies mixed in. Put 4 oz of water in to boil for the couscous on my deck. Started the stove, ran inside to grab a spoon to stir with and it was boiling by the time I got back. Great! Moved the pot aside to let it simmer a bit with the couscous in (3 oz). Mixed in a few (5) cherry tomatoes, some carrot slices, a little bit of white onion, a little garlic and a teaspoon of olive oil into the little pan lid. Put that on and stirred that around for a few minutes. Rotated back to the couscous and then the veggies again one more time. Mixed it all together for a decent sized lunch. Not super filling, but plenty. Could have added plenty more couscous if I was hungrier.

What I didn't like:

The pot and pan cooled almost immediately. Great for cleanup, not so great when you're cooking in both.

The valve control is touchy. Everyone said this about this stove but the problem is not the valve, but the foldout control. As you turn it, if it bends in or out, the gas can turn up or down. With a little practice and focus, it can easily simmer on a low setting.

All in all, I feel like this is a decent set. Should last for plenty of trips where you don't need to cook for anyone else.
text_fidelity_b: Optimus Crux Lite with Tera Solo Cook Set

New Balance Step Counter Pedometer - Belt Clipon Pedometer Fitness Tracker Walking Meter with Removable Base Ideal for Women, Men, Kids to Count Steps, Distance, Calories Burned & Time, Black/Red This step counter doesn't count steps very accurately, and the buttons are easy to bump when unclipping the pedometer so that the step information is reset to zero and lost. There have been many times when testing the best way to use this when the steps showed zero when I checked it. In order to not over count steps due to random movement, the steps are not counted until you've done 10 similar steps in a row. Since I do a lot of work in the kitchen and gardening that is under 10 steps, then a pause, then more steps, this means a lot of steps are not being counted. Also, it seems like it is not counting those first 10 steps, either. If I step 50 steps in a row, it only counts like 32 steps. Frankly, an app on my phone works better than this. I had thought a dedicated device would work better, but I guess not. I will note that it seems to count steps better when this is clipped to my shoe rather than to my waistband. I'll update after little bit if I figure out how to make it work better.

The step counter comes with a battery, and you remove the plastic strip preventing connection in order to turn on the pedometer. It is then constantly on, though it does go into a sleep mode when there is no movement. The instructions that come with it are not very clear, but you're supposed to be able to set things like stride length. You hit the mode button to switch between steps, distance, calories burned, time spent walking, speed, the clock, and total steps. There is also a reset button along one edge and a set button along with other edge. You can remove the counter from the clip (mainly to access the battery chamber). My accidental reset problem has been when the buttons are near the top of the clip, where you have to squeeze to release the clip. I still seem to bump the buttons when the ends are switched, but it's not as often.
text_fidelity_b: New Balance Step Counter Pedometer - Belt Clipon Pedometer Fitness Tracker Walking Meter with Removable Base Ideal for Women, Men, Kids to Count Steps, Distance, Calories Burned & Time, Black/Red

Seattle Seahawks Embroidered Nylon Flag We bought this flag to hang outside of our house on game day. I scoured Amazon for a couple of hours (at least) trying to find the best flag with the best value. I read a lot of reviews on a similar flag, in which most people said the flag was very thin. In my mind, thin does not equal quality, so I was highly drawn towards this flag because it's embroidered. Even though it was double the price, I figured the embroidery was worth it.

We received the flag in the mail pretty quickly, but immediately from its opening, the flag was bleeding color. :( Not sure if it was the thread they used in the embroidery, or the flag itself, but the white part of the Seahawks logo had significant purple coloring on it that looked like it was coming from the edges/embroidery. SUCH A BUMMER. We tried to see if we could wash it off, but it wouldn't come off, so naturally, we returned it. We live in Hawaiʻi where the weather is unpredictable and rains off and on a lot... so we didn't want more bleeding to occur while we hung it outside.

The flag was thick and felt like a durable and good quality material, but the bleeding was obviously a make or break for us. We ended up purchasing the "thin" flag that was half the price of this one and that one is perfect (despite being thin). Not sure if we just got a dud, or what, but based off of our experience, I wouldn't order this again.
text_fidelity_b: Seattle Seahawks Embroidered Nylon Flag

Coleman Sundome Camping Tent, 2/3/4/6 Person Dome Tent with Easy Setup, Included Rainfly and WeatherTec Floor to Block Out Water, 2 Windows and 1 Ground Vent for Air Flow with Charging E-Port Flap I bought this tent in 2017 when I saw it on sale for $39.99 without any intention of using it anytime soon but having one just in case. Due to everything going on this year, I was going nuts being stuck inside so I finally took the plunge and started using it for camping adventures in the Rocky Mountains. So far, so good! I've used this tent 4 separate times now and about 6 nights of sleeping so far. My first trip was a solo one and I had never pitched a tent before by myself. The instructions on the bag tag didn't make the most sense but after about 20 minutes I figured it out on my own. Now I can setup or take down the tent by myself in 5-10 minutes, even less if I have some help.

The included rain-fly is very nice for that purpose as well as providing shade over the mesh openings if you're trying to sleep in a little in the mornings. There are two side windows you can open up for a nice breeze and viewing. Everything zips up nice and easy, however I would advise using both hands when zipping or unzipping the main door. It does have a tendency to catch fabric in the zipper if you're not careful.

I have only slept in the tent by myself so far using a 4" memory foam mattress. Plenty of room for 1-2 people. A family of 3-4 could probably fit comfortably in here with sleeping bags and small children. I don't think 4 adults could sleep too comfortably unless everyone was very cozy with each other.

The included tent stakes are pretty weak. I've already bent almost half of them, so anticipate buying a new set of them at some point. Not a big deal. I had to use rocks to secure my tent better after some high wind gusts blew it around a little bit.

Overall the quality of this tent is very nice and I would buy it again, especially at the price I paid. I see now the price is $69.99 which is probably still a fair price but in that range I would recommend doing some research and seeing if there is a better buy but even at full price this is a good quality tent. So far the coldest I've slept in it was around 40° weather with some light rains and I stayed warm with just a couple blankets, no sleeping bag. I don't know if this would be a good tent for winter camping but I think it would hold up just fine for some late fall snowfall and cold temps when the off-season has begun.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Sundome Camping Tent, 2/3/4/6 Person Dome Tent with Easy Setup, Included Rainfly and WeatherTec Floor to Block Out Water, 2 Windows and 1 Ground Vent for Air Flow with Charging E-Port Flap

We'd seen wedges around and tool a look, finding they supposedly help with squats to support and work the legs more. Okay... but is it a gimmick? In the end I grabbed these Eazy2hD Squat Wedge Block (4PCS) for Heel Elevated Squat to find out and my wife and I are thrilled. Okay, we've only used them a couple times, but so far so good and we are feeling a burn - the good kind. We were both athletes in our younger days and are working to get back into peak form, so we are looking for things that support past injuries in GenX bodies while getting into solid physical health. We took a few minutes each to try these and were both surprised by the support we felt in our knees, hamstrings, and overall legs.

The Eazy2hD Squat Wedge Block (4PCS) for Heel Elevated Squat arrive in a bag - the one you carry them in - inside another bag. This caught us off guard - not the bag, but that whatever was in this bag (we had a few things arriving that day) was SO heavy. What could it be... opened the one to reveal the other and... they're wedges. Wow. We were blown away by the weight, but then talked about it and not having thought about it, realized this would increase safety as you stand and squat down onto these things. Okay, so heavy, check. But substantial, check. Opened the carrying bag - which is a great bonus - keep them together and carry them from room to room, store them in our workout box, whatever, they are well kept. Nice bag.

So pulled them out - there are two, each two pieces. This allows you to adjust the height and such. Now I love to do clay stretching this way - goes back to soccer, baseball, and track days. I was able to get some good stretching here, which is helping me heal a torn hamstring. I felt the burn, but without the pain. I also had pulled another muscle on the same leg that flares every so often, but in doing the squats, I was able to not feel that muscle and it gave me a nice stretch that loosened and warmed up the whole leg.

I have only used them at with the two pieces, not one, so we'll play with them and see. But they did not slip, held their spot on the carpet, and felt great under bare feet - we do both bare and shoed when we workout. There was no discomfort or pain bare footed. But not sure if I'd do longer on them without shoes - no particular reason, just a thought.

We are just starting with these Eazy2hD Squat Wedge Block (4PCS) for Heel Elevated Squat, but so far we are very impressed. If nothing else, the squat is a much "easier" and more comfortable move that feels like we are getting a better workout from than the "old" way of doing it. That alone is worth it to us!

text_fidelity_a:
Sabre Tactical Pepper Gel with Belt Holster for Easy Carry, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Quick Access Flip Top Safety, Tactical Design for Security Professionals, 18 Bursts, 18-Foot Range Every method of self-defense involves a level of awareness and confidence. Exercising "situational awareness" will often allow you to avoid placing yourself in a position where you have to protect yourself. Escape of course is the second option assuming that there is an effective way to avoid a confrontation. But if you are finally forced to bring your use of force to the situation, you must be confident of your method and how to effectively deploy it.

Many years ago I tested a Sabre product for effectiveness. Having a wife and two young daughters motivated me to find something legal that they could carry and use properly without hurting themselves in the process. The particular Sabre unit I tested DID NOT PERFORM AS ADVERTISED! I wrote a poor product review and explained why I came to that conclusion. Unfortunately my review was targeted by numerous individuals who trashed my reasoning and perspective. Yes, the Sabre products have an outstanding reputation. But not every individual unit will work as promised!

About 35 years ago I worked as a product development manager for a company lastly known as We Care America -- formerly Weapons Corporation of America (WCA). One of the products we brought to market was a pepper spray intended for self-defense use. I couldn't put my name on the recommendation until I satisfied myself as to its effectiveness. That meant that I had to be sprayed in the face. Many law enforcement organizations require their officers to be sprayed so that they understand the proper use and deployment of their spray -- and so they know what their targeted individuals will go through.

My suggestion to you is to take your unit outside the house, find an area that is not windy, hold your off-hand away from you with the palm down, and spray the back of your hand a quick burst. You should feel sharp pain on the back of your hand. If you don't, you have a defective unit. If you do, simply wash off with soap and warm water. DO NOT PUT YOUR HANDS NEAR YOUR EYES!

A unit failure can be caused by a short expiration date, poor storage, or less than optimal shipping conditions. Even on this product page Sabre states that other brands experience a 30% failure rate (University of Utah study). If your unit produces the desired irritation, shoot a full burst away from you to get an idea of how well your can is pressurized. Your spray may not go the promised 18 feet. Be aware of its particular limitations. In any event, return it immediately if it doesn't perform as advertised.

Once you determine that your individual unit is effective, make sure to view the offered free training video and then practice deploying your unit without actually spraying it. You must have confidence in both your individual unit and in yourself. Practice may seem redundant but it can be a life saver.
text_fidelity_b: Sabre Tactical Pepper Gel with Belt Holster for Easy Carry, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Quick Access Flip Top Safety, Tactical Design for Security Professionals, 18 Bursts, 18-Foot Range

Black Mountain Products Yoga and Exercise Mat, 1/2 x 73 1/2 x 24 1/2-Inch I bought this mat partly because it is larger than most others. While I really need every inch of it, the dimension of the mat that I have received is actually 1/2 x 71 x 23 3/4 inches, significantly smaller than what is described. The mat is thick and my knees don't hurt anymore as with some 1/4 inches thick mats. But the density of the mat material is not high. It is a bit too soft, too stretchy, and too slippery (between the mat and floor). It is so soft that sometimes it turns into a "J" or "C" shape when I am doing postures on it. When I feet are wide apart on the mat, I can see that the part of the mat between my feet is stretching and the distance between my feet is becoming larger without my moving the feet. This is a bit scary because if the mat rips between my feet I can fall miserably and badly hurt myself.

Today, my yoga teacher saw my mat moving while doing postures on it. She suggested that I better stand on the floor!

The pros:
1. Soft and good cushion.
2. Inexpensive for a 1/2 inches thick mat ($19.99).
3. Black Mountain Products gives a free mat bag.

The cons:
1. Smaller than the size given in product description.
2. Too soft and stretchy due to the low density of the material.
3. Slippery on most floor surfaces.
4. No lighter color options.
text_fidelity_b: Black Mountain Products Yoga and Exercise Mat, 1/2 x 73 1/2 x 24 1/2-Inch

BT Paintball Apex Barrel for Tippmann A5 Not a miracle worker by any means. The idea/concept of being able to shoot your opponents hiding behind trees and in bunkers is great in theory, but hard to execute in real life. That being said, the APEX does what it is supposed to do. Its ramping system creates spin on your ball allowing your shots to curve and bend around objects. The higher the ramp, the less the accuracy. It does increase your distance, significantly, which in my opinion makes the APEX worth it for that alone. The negative is the time it takes to take it off your barrel. With 4 little screws to remove, it's nothing you can do on the field of battle. I made the mistake of using cheap paint and paid the price. Once the paint made it into the APEX after a break, I had to remove myself from the game, get out my screw driver, take off the APEX tip, and douse it with water to clean it out.

At the end of the day, for $25, I'm pleased. Again, not a miracle worker, but allows you some creative shots that will make your opponents "think twice" before camping out behind a tree.
text_fidelity_b: BT Paintball Apex Barrel for Tippmann A5

The only thing that I had to do was pull the safety tab from the battery compartment of the digital display, put the display in its designated spot on the machine, attached the resistance bands, and adjust the step height. The display powers on either when the red button on the display is pushed or when the steps are put in motion, and it will auto shut off after not being used for 4 minutes.  You can easily pick up where you left off by powering on the display, and it retains the info until you reset it.  Resetting the display is easy - just press the red button for a few seconds until the display resets.  The instructions do advise you to place an exercise mat under the machine to protect your floors.  I use this machine every day while I watch TV, and I can see toning in my lower abdomen, thighs, and bottom from it.  I do have to admit that I don't use the resistance bands very often, so I just lay those to the side and do the steps, but I do like that I have the option to use them.  I am NOT an exercise enthusiast - I'm getting older & was advised to be active at least 30 minutes/day, so this was an easy solution for me.  The ONLY improvement that I would make to this machine is having a lighted display.  I have a hard time seeing the display while I'm using the machine because it's somewhat dark.

text_fidelity_a:
Ultimate Survival Technologies BlastMatch Fire Starter Obviously, judging by my profile name, I'm a girl. When it is time for me to start a fire, I need something that works right the first time with my smaller hands and does not break all my short but feminine nails. I have used a number of strikers and fire starters with hilariously varying results. Most are okay-ish. I don't like skinny little strikers that you have to rub with a piece of hacksaw blade which often has a back side that is almost as sharp and jagged as the business end of the blade. I don't like short micro strikers where you end up lighting your hangnails on fire along with the tinder because your hand was so close. (This doesn't actually happen but you get the picture.)

When I first bought this BlastMatch my husband immediately claimed it as his and it disappeared from the face of the earth for over two years. That should have been my first clue that it was the best striker out there. Every once in awhile it would resurface to light the fire pit in the back yard but it would quickly be whisked away to a back pocket and once again vanish from existence as rapidly as it had reappeared. I had no idea where he was hiding it so I simply had to resort to using other strikers I had purchased that worked well enough. They just were not as quick and easy as this one.

Let's talk about what I love. First of all, it has a big, thick firesteel rod that is the thickest I own. (See the picture I uploaded.) This means it will most likely last for the advertised number of strikes. Second, my son has been able to use this to start a fire on our camp outs since he was 7. It's really, really easy. to use. Not really that easy to open but you quickly get the hang of it. Basically you open it, use your thumb to depress the metal scraper on one side and then push down. A bright yellow, orange and white colored shower of sparks will greet you like an angry sparkler gone awry and set alight anything remotely resembling tinder. (A friend who first demonstrated his to us set the fine fibers of our living room rug on fire. After tamping out the little glowing embers, we were sold.)

My husband confiscated the first one I bought and would not so much as let me lay eyes on it so I decided to buy myself a second one. I had given the other crappy fire rods we had somehow picked up along the way to my boy scout son, which was surprisingly safe since they don't hardly light a thing, and proceeded to replace them all with a tool that worked. Since we have one BlastMatch from 2014 and one from 2016, I decided I would compare them side-by-side to see if the product has had any visible changes or become more flimsy as reviewers have insisted. I couldn't find a single difference. The plastic on each was the same thickness, the rod was the same diameter and they both opened with the same springy force.

They give a generous shower of sparks and if you get it anywhere close to a tinder ball, you are going to start a fire with one push. It catches that easily. I am very pleased with BOTH purchases and will continue to use these until they break. (If they do, I'll be right back here to complain.) While we don't use our BlastMatch every single day, we have used the original one somewhere around 50 or more times since my husband is a scout leader and it is still going strong with no cracks in the plastic and no damage visible anywhere to the striker. If you want to be on the safe side, wait until the price drops to twelve or less and then make your purchase. I have seen them as low as ten at various times of the year so your patience can pay off. And do not use your BlastMatch while drunk or trying to impress women. Not that the reviewers who broke theirs were either drunk or able at all to impress women - I'm just giving you some general good advice.

I bought both of my strikers at full price. I do not work for BlastMatch. I don't even particularly like catching things on fire. I just like roasting marshmallows. And Starburst. Happy camping everyone!
text_fidelity_b: Ultimate Survival Technologies BlastMatch Fire Starter

AKOAK Set of 5 Hat Flexible Removable Chin Cord Windproof Strap Clip Adjustable Cord Fastener for Golfing, Fishing, Boating, Sailing, and Other Sports（Black） First, they do what I need them to do. I have an Outdoor Research hat that costs too much to lose to the wind. I wanted something that can stay attached and not interfere with my camera strap, etc. I'm giving four stars because it wasn't useable out of the package for me. Side note: It would be nice if these hat companies would sew small loops to the inside for this purpose.

The cording is elastic/stretchy instead of my preference of non-stretch. As a result....the strap doesn't keep the hat firmly on the head but it does keep it from flying off. The strap is long enough and is comfortable.

The metal ends were too thick to easily punch through the material or through a seam. I didn't want to force the issue and possibly damage my hat.

I made some small loops (can use thin ribbon, upholstery thread, etc) to mount the strap. I made a tight braid out of heavy thread, left the ends very long so I could "sew" them to the inside of the band. I positioned them behind my ears so if my hat does fly forward, my ears will catch the strap.

I can remove the strap to wash the hat, tuck it up out of sight or use it! I would purchase again. They were a reasonable cost.

text_fidelity_a:
WaterRower Club Rowing Machine w/ S4 Monitor & Hi Rise Attachment A few people have complained about putting the Hi-Rise legs on the WaterRower, and they gave it a low rating for that reason. I’m an old lady and I figured out how to do it. I’m writing this review with a few tips to show that it really is EASY. The WaterRower is a fantastic way to keep old tired muscles in shape, and even people who are not that good at DIY (like me) can put it together themselves.

#1 You need a POWER DRILL for the screws (only for the Hi-Rise screws, not for the rest of the WaterRower). Reason is because the screws are going into hard wood. Same “screw hole,” but these are different screws. An “extender” for the screw bit is useful, but may not be necessary (my screw extender is around 4”). Everybody should have a power drill. Borrow one if you don’t have one.

#2 IMPORTANT: The screws to attach the Hi-Rise are not the same screws as for the rubber pads. They are shorter, have a flat head, and different screw threads. You're supposed to get a bag of 16 DIFFERENT screws for the Hi-Rise. If you try to use the screws from the rubber pads that came on the rails, you will not be able to get them into the hard wood, so don’t even try. I ordered my WaterRower from a third party on Amazon, and it was perfect, except that the bag of screws for the Hi-Rise was not included. If that happens, call WaterRower. They sent me a bag of screws, even extra screws, and I got them in the mail the next day.

#3 Get a DRY bar of soap (or some hard wax, like from a candle). Roll the screws back and forth in the dry soap wax to cover as much of the screw’s thread as possible, including the tip of the screw.

#4 You don’t need to drill a pilot hole for the screws because they already have a pilot hole from the screws for the rubber pads that came on the rails. You don’t need to drill the hole bigger.

#5 Use the power drill to slowly drill the screws in as far as they comfortably go, without any strain, then back them out. Do this a few times, in and out, and they will then go all the way in without effort. If you manhandle the screw, it can strip the screw and then you’d have to use Vice-Grips to get the screw out. If you go in and out, slowly, several times, with the soap wax on the screw, it will go all the way in without effort, without any manhandling.

The rest of the assembly of the WaterRower is a breeze. A few people have complained about putting on the Hi-Rise legs, but it sure does make a difference getting on and off the machine, especially if you are an old lady with arthritis in the knees.

ALSO, if you buy from a third party, know that if you call WaterRower, they will register your machine (get the serial number off the back of the meter on it), and you will get two additional years of Warranty for FREE. I was also told, after registering, that the water purification tablets are free, for the lifetime of the machine. They sent me a few extra tablets with the screws.

AND ALSO - please note: I asked WaterRower if it's a good idea to install the Hi-Rise legs first, before assembling the rest of the machine, and they said yes, it's fine, no problem with assembling the rest if you do the Hi-Rise legs first.

If you live within driving distance they will even assemble your machine for you for free, no matter where you bought it, if you have a vehicle that can transport it back home. They can’t ship a fully assembled WaterRower.

The WaterRower people are friendly, helpful, and very accommodating!
text_fidelity_b: WaterRower Club Rowing Machine w/ S4 Monitor & Hi Rise Attachment

That one has a side table attach and sets up/takes down in a different way - folding flat. But when I saw this TR Folding Camping Chair with Cup Holder Leather Padded Arm I decided to grab it because we like the first one so much. We liked the quality, the material, and how nice it feels when sitting. I actually thought this one was going to open/close the same, but missed the design in the product page photos. No worries though - while it opens like so many chairs on the market now, I usually don’t like the style as almost all of the ones I’ve tried hurt across the back of my legs. I’m a shorter guy and they tend to dig into the back of my legs. Not with this TR Folding Camping Chair with Cup Holder Leather Padded Arm - I was pleasantly surprised. When it first arrived I thought I’d blown it, but thrilled to find out I hadn’t - it actually feels great sitting on. Also unlike the other one from this same company, this one does not sit straight up, with a more reclined position. It won’t be as easy to sit at a table and eat, but for relaxing it’s going to be great. Very easy to open and close, the set up of the TR Folding Camping Chair with Cup Holder Leather Padded Arm is as quick as can be. And can set up either fully open, or partially (almost fully) collapsed, making it easy to close and move, or set around waiting to go back into the included bag. The materials are great - thick, the canvas material feels great to sit on. There is a leather (or more likely, leather-like) arm material that also feels nice. Overall, the feel and durability both seem on the spot. I think we’re going to get a lot of years and use out of both chairs. The other one we have has the side table - which is great, but we can set the two next to each other, share the side table, and this one has a pouch on each side - not lined for keeping things cool, but the same material as the chair. Keep your phone, flashlight, keys, or drink in there. The bag fits like the all do and as most do, you’re likely going to need two people to get it in. I was able to get it out on my own no issue, but to hold that bag - which is “tight,” you’re likely better off with an extra set of hands. In the end, we like this TR Folding Camping Chair with Cup Holder Leather Padded Arm as much as the first chair we got from TR, and are thrilled to have added this one. Sigma BC2006MHR DTS Wireless Bicycle Speedometer with Heart Rate Monitor and Altimeter I've had this unit for 6 months. It pretty much works as advertised, but-battery life and magnet strength in Xmitter is questionable. The sender has to be about 1-2 mm from the battery. That's a pretty tight fit, esp with carbon front forks. As the battery on the sender weakens, there's no real communication from it to tell what the problem is (I got a "Too Many Signals" error). On the computer unit, Temperature gauge isn't accurate, reads way too high, and there doesn't seem to be any way to calibrate it. The manual is thorough and detailed, but somehow confusing (What can I say? It's written by English speakers, not English thinkers)
On the positive side, The readout is very clear; you can do individual parameter resets, the rubber bands (o-rings really) are pretty tough, I haven't broken one yet, and it has a dual mount, stem or handlebar, which was very important for me, as I put safety brakes on my handle bar, which ate up real estate. At 120 bucks, it's pricey, but at 83? IMO that's getting into bargain territory for the feature set.
text_fidelity_b: Sigma BC2006MHR DTS Wireless Bicycle Speedometer with Heart Rate Monitor and Altimeter

I had too many flats. I've never found a 12.5 inch "thorn-resistant" inner tube in this size so this tube seems to be as good as it gets. Plus all the 12.5" tires are less than heavy-duty so the entire 12.5" system is prone to flats.

My solution is to use these tubes along with "Mr. Tuffy" or "Earthguard"-brand tire inserts, both available here on Amazon. The size for BMX fits well enough. Haven't had a flat since.

Without the angled valve stem you will struggle unnecessarily every time you try to inflate your tubes.

[Edit: I recently (10/13) found 12.5" tubes in "thorn-resistant" here on Amazon but they didn't have the angled valve stem so the inserts are still the best solution.]

However, I really wish they'd included some directions as it's an experimental, hit-and-miss method of trying to use them. Also, one of the two sticks won't lock. One stick is fine--I could unscrew the pole (twist the pole, not the black part between the segments), pull the length out, and screw until locked on both the bottom and top segments of the stick. It only took about 4-5 twists to unlock and then again to lock this pole. The second one locks on the bottom section, but that's only tall enough for a child. The top portion won't lock even after being twisted in the lock direction for several minutes. That stick decreases in height with every step and so is useless, thus the low star rating. I can unlock and collapse both poles without problem.

The tip can be used with a 1" textured, rubber tip attachment for sidewalks and such. This tip simply pulls off to expose the permanent, (3/16" across) tungsten carbide tip. A 2" wide plastic disk can be slipped over the tip and screwed into place about 2" up the pole to prevent the stick from sinking too far in sand. There is an adjustable, padded wrist strap. The sticks are a lightweight metal and seem reasonably sturdy. You have to keep track of any tip attachments when not using them as they don't come with a pouch or container.

text_fidelity_a:
Henderson Women's Thermoprene 3mm Front Zip Shorty Springsuit, Black/Lavender, 8 I got my first Henderson Zip Shorty a couple years ago for snorkelling on the Big Island. It was SUPERB! There is simply no easier style for getting into and out of a wetsuit on hot, steamy days or peeling them off when they're all wet. It's super easy to step into one of the legs and then zip the shorty up as high as you like. There is JUST the right amount of give in the armpits so you can swim but not fill the suit with water. It's a brilliant design, actually. The 3mm thickness was absolutely perfect for swimming in HI's water - where temps averaged 71-74F for us.

After each use, I'd faithfully soak, then rinse the suit out with special neoprene detergent, then roll it in a beach towel and hang it up to dry in the shower stall. It would be clean, fresh, dry and ready to use within a couple hours - even in a humid place.

I wore a long-sleeved rashguard under mine for extra sun protection, but otherwise, was totally warm enough with great flexibility for swimming in this garment. At the end of our 3-mo stay in HI, I donated my Henderson - and the dive shop nearly cried for joy!

Flash forward 2 years, and I bought the identical suit for snorkelling on Kauai! If I was psychic, I never would've donated the last one, and now I'm going to be an optimist and keep this one!

CAVEAT!!! Be sure to soak, WASH, rinse your suit out before you try it on - seriously! I just wore mine for 10-15 min day one and woke up later that night with a shorty-shaped RASH on my skin. I only read about neoprene reactions after that - and immediately washed my new shorty. Err on the cautious side, cuz that was the one and only time I got a rash, and you can avoid that if you just wash it first.

Of course, if you don't want to remove the tags, you could also try your wetsuit on with a "skin" underneath - but be sure to wash that garment then to avoid any neoprene reaction.
text_fidelity_b: Henderson Women's Thermoprene 3mm Front Zip Shorty Springsuit, Black/Lavender, 8

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon COOLSHOT 40 Golf Laser Rangefinder Works great and is 2/3 or less the price of a comparable Bushnell range finder. I give this 4 instead of 5 stars only because the optics are somewhat sensitive and require the unit to be precisely in front of your pupil to be able to see well. More expensive optics have a slightly more forgiving area in which the image is easily viewed.

More generally, the unit finds targets quickly and appears to generate the same distances as more expensive Bushnell finders. The Nikon may be very slightly slower than the Bushnell at locating a flag stick instead of trees behind it, but I'm talking about 2 seconds instead of 1 second... hardly enough to delay your golf round. The comparable Bushnell range finders are technically better, but can be close to double the price. This Nikon works extremely well. Potentially the biggest problem with the Nikon relative to Bushnell range finders is they are less common. You will have a more difficult time finding accessories like carrying cases and friends who borrow your range finder to shoot a distance are more likely to have to ask you questions about how it works. If you want the absolute best and finest that all your friends can use and that has a bigger selection of third party accessories, get the Bushnell. If you want to save $200 and get a very high performing range finder for yourself, this Nikon is perfect.
text_fidelity_b: Nikon COOLSHOT 40 Golf Laser Rangefinder

My kids were putting the disposable hand warmers ('hotties', the kind you shake up to activate) on their faces and it made me realize how toxic those must be, and how much trash we are making by using them. This particular item is one of the fancier ones we've purchased. I got the pink color; it is shimmery pink, and the part that goes around the outside of the hand warmer is a shiny, metalic looking pink (although it is plastic). It serves as a hand warmer, a flashlight, a power pack (comes with cord), and a vibrating massager.

- Press the button once for power (four blue indicator lights show battery life)
- Press and hold for heat (press again to change between 3 heat levels)
- Press twice for flash light
- Press three times for vibration

Once you're using the heat setting, you'll see it starts you off at the highest setting (60- this one is too hot for me). I usually use the middle (50) or low (40) heat settings. I like that it has a wrist strap for added security. I'll also add that the size of this item is bigger than others we have so it doesn't fit as well in my hands but is a good size for my husband. The size probably also contributes to it's power and longevity of the battery pack. As for weight, the difference is negligible. My whole family loves these electronic, rechargable hand warmers and we don't leave the house without them anymore now that it is cold (the cold has not slowed down my kids from playing outside for hours at a time)!
text_fidelity_b: MZTDYTL Hand Warmers Rechargeable,10000mAh Electric USB Reusable Hand Warmer,4-in-1 Function Double-Sided 3-Levels Heating Pocket Hand Warmer-Outdoor Sports Winter Warm Gifts for Women Men Girls Boys

text_fidelity_a:
OKAI EA10 Electric Scooter with Seat, Up to 25-35 Miles Range & 15.5MPH, Moped Scooter Bike for Adults with 10 Inch Vacuum Tires Set up of the scooter is a fairly simple process. The only downside is putting on the bike seat. It doesn’t slide down very easily and isn’t fully secure, the seat swivels back and forth which can be inconvenient.

The scooter in general is great and able to take me from point A to point B in a timely manner. One feature that really makes the scooter user friendly is the battery. Being able to take the battery out and leave the scooter outside while charging it inside is extremely convenient.

The keys that come with the scooter are also extremely convenient. With the NFC feature it’s easy to unlock, all you have to do is touch the key to the scooter’s digital interface.

Making sure you have enough battery is important if you are planning on going somewhere far. The gauge on the scooter doesn’t give you an accurate idea of how far you can go, and the apps percentages aren’t very accurate either.

One other thing I wish it had was a longer pole. It is tall enough for my hand to reach it when I’m standing but it has to be fully extended so it can be awkward and unsafe. If it was a little bit longer, it’d be perfect for sitting and standing.

It is most comfortable to ride while sitting but you are able to stand. Depending on your height, standing may feel comfortable or a bit awkward. If you’re around the 6ft range it feels slightly too short to use while standing, although it is possible. It would've been nice if some adjustments have been made in the scooter so that it would have been easy to use both sitting and standing.

The scooter is really easy to operate. Right out of the box, all you do is turn it on and go. The acceleration is quick and the brakes are fast and efficient.

The scooter is made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 700 bucks I'm sure it's at least 250 bucks over priced.
text_fidelity_b: OKAI EA10 Electric Scooter with Seat, Up to 25-35 Miles Range & 15.5MPH, Moped Scooter Bike for Adults with 10 Inch Vacuum Tires
